status: Source-informed development visual review; not historical qualification
source_figures: LIB31 front main bearing and housing oil leads
findings: The isometric exposes the installed shaft and all seven bearing stations by hiding only the upper casting in the view. Both castings remain physically installed. Engine support context is retained.

The bare forging visibly has six paired throws and hollow main/pin ends; webs have controlled rounded outlines. End projection places1/6 upper-left,2/5 lower-left,3/4 lower-right consistent withLIB93.

Localized crossed grooves now match the feature type inLIB31. Two front oil entries, central dowel hole and joint notches are visible. The previous continuous inner grooves were rejected despite green fit checks.

The shorter bearing now has a rounded local oil pocket, as opposed to a complete circumferential running-face groove. Pocket dimensions/clocking and upper-shell transfer remain estimates; no pixel fit claimed.
The double thrust section exposes three races, two ball rows/cages, sleeves and nose housing. Counts and internal dimensions remain commercial-part approximations, not printed-source dimensions.

The revised Z-section exposes the taper key, two extraction holes, retaining screw, output nut and cotter inside the existing flywheel. The source-length screw tip reaches the estimated shaft hollow; revisit cavity sizing with the nose plug/stud.

The longitudinal half-section shows hollow journals, integral case webs and separated dry gear floor. Offset pins project behind the shaft centerline in this view; independent void witnesses are needed to distinguish projection from material.

Engine axial registration, crank-key angular registration, forging fillets, bearing machining detail, six-versus-seven mounts and complete source fits remain unqualified. Shaft plugs/gear/locking hardware and cylinders/rods/services remain pending.

After the spherical-pocket parametrization repair, all eight current views were inspected directly. Seven are byte-identical to the previous reviewed native renderings; only thrust_section.png changes tessellation. The section retains two rows of balls, their cages, three races and two sleeves with no visible material distortion.

The short-bearing source sketch places the pocket and locating feature near the joint; the current location and pocket outline remain an explicit approximation. This comparison accepts the feature family for development, not an exact recovered machining drawing.
